question: How can we discover novel therapeutic targets for rare genetic disorders?
description: Applying cross-disease mechanism discovery for orphan indications
key_contradictions: Patients with same mutation have different severity
Why do some genetic defects show no phenotype?
Variable penetrance in familial rare diseases

benchmark_hypotheses.statement: The variable penetrance in rare genetic diseases is mediated by a threshold-dependent compensatory pathway that activates only when modifier gene expression falls below a critical level, explaining why identical mutations can have opposite outcomes in different individuals.
What if the lack of phenotype in some genetic knockouts is not due to redundancy but to an adaptive rewiring that creates an emergent property only visible under stress conditions?

Phenotypic similarity between disparate rare diseases connects through a hidden mediator - a master regulator of proteostasis that when perturbed creates convergent downstream effects despite different upstream causes.
